quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.
Bumps in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Buckle your safety belt.
Make sure all passengers buckle their safety belts.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Make it a habit before driving. Buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same before starting the car.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: How can you avoid getting drowsy on long trips?

options.text: Turn on the car radio.
Drive slower.
Stop and rest at regular times.
Move your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest at regular times.
questions.explanation: On long trips, stop regularly to rest and stretch. You don't have to wait until you feel tired.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always let pedestrians cross safely. Be careful around pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: How should you pass another vehicle?

options.text: Wait for a signal from the other driver.
Change lanes quickly so the other driver sees you.
Signal and pass when it is safe to do so.
Stay close behind the vehicle to pass faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and pass when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: When it is safe and legal to pass, signal your turn. Check your mirrors and look over your left shoulder before moving into the left lane.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this road sign?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign with black markings warns drivers that a divided highway is starting. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: When should you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?

options.text: At night.
During the day.
Only under ideal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive under perfect conditions. Always drive at a safe speed for the current conditions. All drivers must drive safely.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not pass.
Do not enter.
No turn on red.
Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is ahead. The road will split into two separate one-way roads with a divider between them. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red lights and gates are active.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger signals you to stop, if there is a stop sign, or if flashing red lights and gates are operating.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, what should you do?

options.text: You must yield to pedestrians.
Pedestrians must yield to you.
Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings. You must stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked.

questions.question: Which statement is true about weather and driving?

options.text: Sudden weather changes mean you need to change how you drive.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you in bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Adjust your driving when weather changes suddenly. Slow down in rain and fog. Watch for fast vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always stop and let pedestrians cross. Be ready to stop whenever you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful where children are present.

questions.question: Which of these does alcohol affect?

options.text: How fast your eyes recover from headlight glare
How fast you can react
How you judge distances
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, affects your vision, and changes how you judge speed and distance. It is especially dangerous at night because alcohol reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, what ensures you drive safely?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home from a friend who hasn't been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home from a friend who hasn't been drinking.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to ride home with a friend who doesn't drink. Coffee and cold showers don't reduce alcohol's effects. Your body takes about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: There is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.
Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians even if there is no crosswalk. Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing in any area, marked or unmarked.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Dark areas you see when you get tired.
Areas near your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show.
Traffic control signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas near your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. When changing lanes, turn your head to look over your shoulder to check these areas near the rear corners of your vehicle.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic going straight. Always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: The traffic light turns yellow as you near an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass before the red light.
Brake hard to stop immediately.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the light will turn red soon. Be prepared to stop safely before the intersection if you can.
